title: Graphs, Predictions & Trends
pedagogicalStatus: Unreviewed draft: formative practice only; CEFR mastery disabled.

sources.title: A virtual cart: distance–time graph
paragraphs: A computer simulation shows a cart moving in a straight line. The horizontal axis is Time (s). The vertical axis is Position (m). The plotted points are (0 s, 0 m), (1 s, 2 m), (2 s, 4 m), (3 s, 6 m), and (4 s, 8 m). The line rises at a steady rate. The model speed is 2 m/s during these four seconds. The graph does not show what actually happens after four seconds. A student may predict later positions only if the constant-speed assumption continues.
**Visual accessibility:** supply text summary, keyboard-accessible data table, descriptive chart title and visual labels; do not rely on colors alone.

sources.title: A model temperature graph
paragraphs: An educational cooling model displays 32 °C at zero minutes, 30 °C after two minutes, 28 °C after four minutes and 26 °C after six minutes. The horizontal axis shows Time (min) and the vertical axis shows Temperature (°C). The line goes down during the recorded interval. It falls by 2 °C every two minutes in the displayed data. The text does not give a new value after six minutes. The graph describes a simulation, not a physical measurement.
**Visual accessibility:** supply text summary, keyboard-accessible data table, descriptive chart title and visual labels; do not rely on colors alone.

sources.title: An ideal resistor: a current–voltage graph
paragraphs: A virtual circuit contains an ideal 20 Ω resistor. The displayed current values are 0 A at 0 V, 0.10 A at 2 V, 0.20 A at 4 V and 0.30 A at 6 V. The horizontal axis shows Voltage (V) and the vertical axis shows Current (A). The points make a rising straight line. At a fixed resistance, the model current increases as voltage increases. The values are results of the ideal model, not physical laboratory data.
**Visual accessibility:** supply text summary, keyboard-accessible data table, descriptive chart title and visual labels; do not rely on colors alone.

sources.title: A horizontal graph and an incomplete label
paragraphs: In a class activity, a virtual sensor displays a constant temperature of 22 °C at 0, 2 and 4 minutes. A student draws a horizontal line. The student first writes only “Time” on the horizontal axis. The tutor asks the student to add the unit: “Time (min).” The vertical axis already says “Temperature (°C).” A horizontal line describes an unchanged value in the displayed interval. It does not prove the value will stay unchanged forever.
**Visual accessibility:** supply text summary, keyboard-accessible data table, descriptive chart title and visual labels; do not rely on colors alone.
